label: <DEL> in length-3 sequences (step 3/4 only)
explanation: Fires only at steps t=3 and t=4 and never during the copy phase. About 74% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step of short sequences: L=3 (about 65% of mass, rate 60% at that step) and, more weakly, L=4 at t=4. The other 26% is at t=3 in the original phase (the 4th original token) when that token is o, a, r or u. Whether it fires and how strongly depends gradedly on which tokens came before: s, t, z, h, p, l, k and the digits 1/2 raise both the rate and the magnitude (the top activations are all L=3 <DEL> steps after prefixes containing s/t/z/p/h). Prefixes made only of vowels or letters like c/q/i/m/d usually do not fire. It almost never fires on repeated tokens (in_first=0). Because this token dependence is graded rather than a clean set, the simple predicate has precision about 0.6 and misses the original-phase t=3 firings, which are low precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: L=4 & t=4 (+6.17), t=3 & in_tok=o (+5.56), t=3 (+5.11), t=3 & in_tok=a (+4.20), t=3 & in_tok=r (+3.56), prev2_tok=s (+3.54). Lower it: orig1=o (-3.24), prev_tok=o (-3.13), prev2_tok=a (-3.08), prev_tok=d (-2.90).
